name: Canadian wildfires
headline: Prolonged July heat and dryness; in the week beginning 20 July 2026 widespread lightning storms triggered numerous new fires (WWA, citing The Guardian and Reuters).

sections.The trigger: Prolonged July heat and dryness; in the week beginning 20 July 2026 widespread lightning storms triggered numerous new fires (WWA, citing The Guardian and Reuters).
sections.What amplified it: 3M+ ha burned; about 94% of the area burned up to the time of the WWA study (published 6 August 2026) burned in the five weeks from the end of June to the end of July (WWA, citing CWFIS); smoke brought dangerous air quality to parts of the Midwest and Northeast United States where more than 120 million people live (WWA, citing CNN).
sections.Climate signal: WWA (6 August 2026): climate change made extreme fire weather like that of July 2026 about 5 times more likely in the Northwest Territories (7-day measure) and about 2 times more likely (30-day measure there, and both measures in Ontario): a result about fire weather conditions, not about fires.
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
